items.title: BCA in Cloud Computing & Cyber Security
items.text: Programme: BCA in Cloud Computing & Cyber Security. Level: degree. Duration: 3 years. Eligibility: 10+2 pass in any stream. No entrance test required. A UGC-recognised bachelor degree built around industry certification. Students work on cloud infrastructure and security tooling from the first year, with placement support beginning before the degree completes. What you can do after it: Graduate with a recognised BCA degree plus stacked industry certifications; Build and secure cloud infrastructure on major providers; Enter roles such as Cloud Support Associate, SOC Analyst, or Network Engineer. Modules covered: Foundations of computing and networking; Linux system administration; Cloud infrastructure and virtualisation; Cyber security operations and incident response; Industry capstone project. Industry certifications: Red Hat, CompTIA, Cloud platform associate.

items.title: Cyber Security Specialist Programme
items.text: Programme: Cyber Security Specialist Programme. Level: diploma. Duration: 12 months. Eligibility: 10+2 pass, or graduates and working professionals seeking a career change. A hands-on programme covering defensive and offensive security practice, built for learners who want to move into a security operations role without a multi-year degree commitment. What you can do after it: Operate as a Tier-1 SOC analyst; Run vulnerability assessments and interpret findings; Prepare for recognised industry security certifications. Modules covered: Networking and protocol fundamentals; Operating system hardening; Threat detection and SIEM operations; Ethical hacking and penetration testing basics; Governance, risk and compliance overview. Industry certifications: CompTIA Security+, Red Hat.

items.title: Cloud & DevOps Engineer Programme
items.text: Programme: Cloud & DevOps Engineer Programme. Level: diploma. Duration: 10 months. Eligibility: Graduates or working professionals with basic IT familiarity. Designed for upskillers already in an IT role. Covers cloud infrastructure, containerisation and CI/CD pipelines with an emphasis on production practice rather than theory. What you can do after it: Deploy and operate containerised workloads; Build CI/CD pipelines end to end; Move into Cloud Engineer or DevOps Associate roles. Modules covered: Linux and shell proficiency; Cloud compute, storage and networking; Containers and orchestration; CI/CD tooling and automation; Infrastructure as code. Industry certifications: Red Hat, Cloud platform associate.

items.title: Network & Infrastructure Engineer Programme
items.text: Programme: Network & Infrastructure Engineer Programme. Level: diploma. Duration: 9 months. Eligibility: 10+2 pass. No prior IT experience required. The classic Jetking networking track, updated for hybrid cloud environments. Suited to learners who want a structured entry into IT infrastructure roles. What you can do after it: Configure and troubleshoot enterprise networks; Administer Windows and Linux server environments; Enter roles such as Network Support Engineer or IT Infrastructure Associate. Modules covered: Networking fundamentals and routing; Windows server administration; Linux server administration; Network security essentials; Hybrid cloud connectivity. Industry certifications: CompTIA Network+, Red Hat.

items.title: AI & Cloud Applications Track
items.text: Programme: AI & Cloud Applications Track. Level: certification. Duration: 6 months. Eligibility: Graduates, or learners who have completed a Jetking foundation programme. A shorter, focused track on applying AI services within cloud environments — aimed at learners who already have infrastructure grounding and want to add applied AI capability. What you can do after it: Integrate managed AI services into applications; Understand model deployment and cost considerations; Add an applied AI specialisation to an infrastructure profile. Modules covered: Cloud AI service landscape; Working with model APIs; Data handling and pipelines; Deployment, monitoring and cost control. Industry certifications: Cloud platform AI associate.

items.title: IT Foundation Programme
items.text: Programme: IT Foundation Programme. Level: short. Duration: 4 months. Eligibility: 10th pass or above. Absolute beginners welcome. An entry point for learners with no technical background, covering computing fundamentals, networking basics and the study habits needed for a longer programme. What you can do after it: Build confidence with computing and networking fundamentals; Identify which specialist track fits your goals; Progress into a diploma or degree programme. Modules covered: Computing fundamentals; Introduction to networking; Introduction to operating systems; Career orientation and pathway planning.

items.title: What is the eligibility for the BCA in Cloud Computing & Cyber Security?
items.text: Question: What is the eligibility for the BCA in Cloud Computing & Cyber Security? Answer: You need to have passed 10+2 in any stream. There is no entrance test for admission to the programme.

items.title: Is there an entrance exam?
items.text: Question: Is there an entrance exam? Answer: Jetking programmes do not require an entrance test. Admission is based on eligibility criteria for the specific programme, and a counsellor will confirm your fit during the enquiry conversation.

items.title: How much do the courses cost?
items.text: Question: How much do the courses cost? Answer: Fees vary by programme, centre and intake, so they are confirmed by a counsellor rather than published as a single figure. EMI options are available on most programmes.

items.title: Are instalment or EMI options available?
items.text: Question: Are instalment or EMI options available? Answer: EMI options are available on most programmes. The specific arrangements depend on the centre and the programme, and a counsellor will walk you through what applies to your case.

items.title: Can I study while working full time?
items.text: Question: Can I study while working full time? Answer: Several centres run evening and weekend batches specifically for working professionals. Availability varies by centre, so it is worth checking with the centre nearest you.

items.title: Can I join without any technical background?
items.text: Question: Can I join without any technical background? Answer: Yes. The IT Foundation Programme is designed for learners with no prior technical experience, and it leads into the longer diploma and degree tracks.

items.title: What does placement support include?
items.text: Question: What does placement support include? Answer: Placement support covers interview preparation, profile building and introductions to hiring employers. Specific outcomes depend on the programme, the centre and the individual learner, so a counsellor can give you the picture for the centre you are considering.

items.title: Which industry certifications are included?
items.text: Question: Which industry certifications are included? Answer: Programmes are built around recognised industry certifications including Red Hat and CompTIA tracks. The exact certifications included depend on the programme you choose.

items.title: Where are Jetking centres located?
items.text: Question: Where are Jetking centres located? Answer: Jetking operates centres across India. You can browse centres by city to find the one nearest you, along with the programmes each centre offers.

items.title: How do I enquire about a Jetking franchise?
items.text: Question: How do I enquire about a Jetking franchise? Answer: Franchise enquiries go through a dedicated team. Submitting the franchise enquiry form starts a conversation about territory availability, the operating model and what partnership involves.

items.title: What is the profile of a Jetking Franchisee?
items.text: Question: What is the profile of a Jetking Franchisee? Answer: Jetking franchisees typically include: (1) existing entrepreneurs looking for new opportunities in the education business, (2) professionals with 5–7 years of work experience in any industry, and (3) engineers or MBA graduates with a passion to work in the education business.

items.title: Who will build my centre? Can I use my existing centre?
items.text: Question: Who will build my centre? Can I use my existing centre? Answer: We will help you build your centre. You can also use your existing setup, provided it matches Jetking’s specifications.

items.title: What are the responsibilities of a Franchise?
items.text: Question: What are the responsibilities of a Franchise? Answer: As a Jetking franchise, you will be responsible for: (1) investing to set up the training centre as per Jetking specifications, (2) managing and operating the centre daily, (3) following standard operating procedures and conducting training as per Jetking guidelines, (4) creating strong student word-of-mouth by delivering good quality training and good placements, and (5) generating business through multiple marketing activities in your local area.

items.title: Can I own more than one Franchisee?
items.text: Question: Can I own more than one Franchisee? Answer: Yes. Depending upon your performance, you can open another Jetking franchise in any location.

items.title: Will I be trained to run a Jetking franchise?
items.text: Question: Will I be trained to run a Jetking franchise? Answer: Yes. We provide training on A–Z of the education business. This includes training for marketing, branding, technology, delivery, recruitment and other support required for day-to-day operations of your learning centre.

items.title: What kind of technical training will I receive as a franchise?
items.text: Question: What kind of technical training will I receive as a franchise? Answer: Technical training is provided to your faculty members so they can conduct batches. We also run training programmes to upskill the faculties from time to time.

items.title: Who enforces quality at Jetking?
items.text: Question: Who enforces quality at Jetking? Answer: Jetking is ISO 9001:2015 certified and operates through a comprehensive Quality Management Program. Alongside ISO processes, the QMP supports continual improvement in centre operations and delivers customer satisfaction.

items.title: How do I start a Jetking Franchise?
items.text: Question: How do I start a Jetking Franchise? Answer: Jetking works according to a quality management system and a comprehensive Quality Management Program that supports continual improvement for centre operations. This helps deliver student satisfaction and centre performance.

items.title: How long do the programmes take?
items.text: Question: How long do the programmes take? Answer: Programme length ranges from a 4-month foundation course to a 3-year BCA degree. Diploma programmes typically run between 9 and 12 months.

items.title: What is the difference between the cloud and cyber security tracks?
items.text: Question: What is the difference between the cloud and cyber security tracks? Answer: Cloud programmes focus on building and operating infrastructure, while cyber security programmes focus on defending it — detecting threats and responding to incidents. Both share networking and operating system fundamentals, and a counsellor can help you decide which suits your goals.

items.title: Starting a cloud computing career after 12th: what the first three years look like — Starting a cloud computing career after 12th: what the first three years look like
items.text: A realistic walkthrough of the path from finishing school to a first cloud role — what you study, when you start applying, and what employers actually check. Choosing a technical path straight after 12th is less about picking the trendiest term and more about understanding what the first job actually asks of you. Cloud roles at entry level are operational: you are keeping systems running, responding to alerts, and learning the specific environment your employer uses.

items.title: Starting a cloud computing career after 12th: what the first three years look like — Year one: fundamentals that do not go out of date
items.text: Networking and operating systems are the foundation. Every cloud platform is an abstraction over these, and troubleshooting almost always resolves down to them. Learners who skip this stage tend to stall when something breaks in a way the tutorial did not cover. How networks route traffic, and how to read what went wrong. Linux command line fluency — not memorised commands, but comfort. How virtualisation underpins everything a cloud provider sells you

items.title: Starting a cloud computing career after 12th: what the first three years look like — Year two: specialisation and certification
items.text: This is where the cloud and security tracks separate. Both remain employable; they suit different temperaments. Cloud work rewards people who enjoy building and automating. Security work rewards people who enjoy investigating.

items.title: Starting a cloud computing career after 12th: what the first three years look like — Year three: the job search starts before you finish
items.text: The most common mistake is treating placement as something that begins after the final exam. Internships, project work and certification all carry more weight with employers than the completion date on a certificate.

items.title: Cyber security or cloud computing: how to tell which one suits you — Cyber security or cloud computing: how to tell which one suits you
items.text: These two tracks look similar from outside and feel very different from inside. A practical way to choose, based on the work rather than the job title. Prospective students routinely ask which of these two pays more. It is the wrong question — the pay bands overlap heavily at entry level. The better question is which kind of day you want.

items.title: Cyber security or cloud computing: how to tell which one suits you — The shape of the work
items.text: Cloud engineering is constructive. You are building, automating and improving systems, and the feedback loop is that something works better than it did. Security is investigative and adversarial. You are looking for what is wrong, often under time pressure, and the feedback loop is that nothing bad happened. People who enjoy finishing things tend to prefer cloud. People who enjoy finding things tend to prefer security.

items.title: Cyber security or cloud computing: how to tell which one suits you — What both require
items.text: Solid networking fundamentals — non-negotiable for either. Comfort with Linux. Willingness to keep learning after the certification is signed

items.title: Switching into IT in your thirties: what actually transfers — Switching into IT in your thirties: what actually transfers
items.text: Career changers consistently underestimate how much of their existing experience counts. A look at what transfers, what does not, and how to sequence the change. The anxiety most career changers bring is that they are starting from zero. In practice, they are not — but the things that transfer are rarely the things they expect.

items.title: Switching into IT in your thirties: what actually transfers — What transfers
items.text: Working professionally: meeting deadlines, escalating clearly, handling a difficult stakeholder. Domain knowledge — a banking background is a genuine advantage in BFSI security roles. Judgement about what matters, which is the hardest thing to teach a fresh graduate

items.title: Switching into IT in your thirties: what actually transfers — What does not
items.text: Technical fundamentals have to be built properly. There is no shortcut here, and attempting one produces the most common failure mode: a candidate who can operate a tool but cannot diagnose why it stopped working.

items.title: Switching into IT in your thirties: what actually transfers — Sequencing the change
items.text: Most successful changers do not resign first. Evening or weekend batches, then a period of overlap, then the move. It takes longer and it works more often.

items.title: Seven questions parents should ask any IT training institute — Seven questions parents should ask any IT training institute
items.text: A checklist for families evaluating technical training — the questions that separate a substantive programme from a well-marketed one. Parents funding a technical programme are making a significant decision with limited technical context. These questions are designed to be answerable by any institute acting in good faith. What is the recognition status of the qualification, and who recognises it?. What proportion of the last completed batch was placed, and where?. What is the total cost, including certification and examination fees?. Who teaches, and what is their industry background?. What does placement support actually consist of — is it introductions, or is it training?. What happens if my child struggles partway through?. Can I speak to a recent graduate?

items.title: Seven questions parents should ask any IT training institute — On placement claims
items.text: Ask for the denominator. A placement percentage is only meaningful alongside how many students it was calculated from and whether it counts students who did not complete the programme. A serious institute will answer all seven without hesitation. Reluctance on any of them is itself information.

items.title: The DevOps skills employers are actually screening for — The DevOps skills employers are actually screening for
items.text: Job descriptions list twenty tools. Interviews test about four things. Here is the gap, and what to prioritise. DevOps job descriptions have become inventories of every tool the team has ever touched. Interview processes are far narrower, and understanding that difference saves months of misdirected study.

items.title: The DevOps skills employers are actually screening for — What gets tested
items.text: Can you debug a failing pipeline you did not write?. Do you understand what a container actually is, beyond the commands?. Can you reason about a production incident under questioning?. Do you write automation that someone else can maintain?

items.title: The DevOps skills employers are actually screening for — What rarely gets tested
items.text: Tool-specific syntax recall. Interviewers assume documentation exists. Depth in one toolchain consistently beats shallow familiarity with six.

items.title: What running an IT training franchise involves — What running an IT training franchise involves
items.text: An honest look at the operating reality of a training centre — the work, the local dynamics, and where new franchise partners typically underestimate effort. Prospective franchise partners generally arrive with a financial model and an underdeveloped picture of the operating work. The model matters, but the operating work determines whether the model holds.

items.title: What running an IT training franchise involves — The work is local
items.text: Enrolment is driven by relationships with schools, colleges and local employers in your catchment. National brand recognition opens the conversation; it does not close the admission.

items.title: What running an IT training franchise involves — Where partners underestimate
items.text: Faculty recruitment and retention in a competitive local market. Counsellor capability — it is a specialist skill, not general sales. The seasonality of admissions cycles and the cash-flow discipline it requires Partners who treat the centre as an operating business rather than a passive investment consistently perform better.

items.text: Admissions policy. How Jetking evaluates eligibility and enrols students across centres. Admissions are handled at the centre level. Counsellors verify eligibility against the published programme requirements and guide applicants through documentation and batch selection. Eligibility Each programme lists its own eligibility on the course page. Degree tracks typically require completion of Class 12; short certifications may accept working professionals with relevant experience.

items.text: Refund & fee policy. High-level fee and refund guidance. Exact figures are centre-specific. Programme fees vary by centre and batch. Published fee figures on the site are structured data only when Jetking has authorised disclosure. For a quote, speak to a counsellor at your nearest centre.

items.text: Ananya Sharma, Lead Instructor — Cloud & Cyber Security. Ananya teaches cloud architecture and defensive security modules across degree and professional tracks, with a focus on lab-led certification prep. Specialisations: Cloud, Cyber Security, AWS.

items.text: Placement support. Jetking counsellors and placement teams help students prepare for interviews and connect with hiring partners. Placement support includes resume workshops, mock interviews, and introductions to hiring partners where available. Results depend on the student, the market, and the programme.
